questions.stem_latex:
Wind turbines, such as those shown, are used to generate power.

\exfigure{1228_q13_1}

In theory, the power that could be generated by a wind turbine is modelled using the equation

$$T = 20\,000w^3,$$

where

$T$ is the theoretical power generated, in watts

$w$ is the speed of the wind, in metres per second

parts.label: a
parts.latex: Using this equation, what is the theoretical power generated by a wind turbine if the wind speed is $7.3$ m/s?

parts.label: b
parts.latex:
In practice, the actual power generated by a wind turbine is only 40% of the theoretical power.

If $A$ is the actual power generated, in watts, write an equation for $A$ in terms of $w$.

parts.label: c
d
parts.latex:
A particular farm requires at least 4.4 million watts of actual power in order to be self-sufficient.

What is the minimum wind speed required for the farm to be self-sufficient?

parts.label: e
parts.latex:
A more accurate formula to calculate the power ($P$) generated by a wind turbine is

$$P = 0.61 \times \pi \times r^2 \times w^3,$$

where

$r$ is the length of each blade, in metres

$w$ is the speed of the wind, in metres per second

Each blade of a particular wind turbine has a length of 43 metres. The turbine operates at a wind speed of 8 m/s.

Using the formula above, if the wind speed increased by 10%, what would be the percentage increase in the power generated by this wind turbine?

solutions.latex: The maximum amount of boots is 120, so $x$ cannot be greater than 120.

At $w = 9$:

$A = 5.8$ million watts (from graph)

$T = 14.6$ million watts (from graph)

Difference: $14.6 - 5.8 = 8.8$ million watts

OR at $w = 9$:

$T = 20\,000 \times 9^3 = 14\,580\,000$ watts

$A = 8000 \times 9^3 = 5\,832\,000$ watts

Difference $= 14\,580\,000 - 5\,832\,000 = 8\,748\,000$ watts

notes: Paper: The King's School Y12 Mathematics Standard 2 AT2, March 2020. Solutions bundled as a hand-annotated copy (pages 22-36); MCQ key read from the filled answer sheet (page 23). Section II header prints '42 marks' but the cover and question marks give 39 (9: 8, 10: 4, 11: 8, 12: 10, 13: 9); cover total used. Q9 split into 9(a) and 9(b) as unrelated; the question numbers 11 and 12 split into (a),(b),(c) as unrelated. Q9(b) prints an extra '1' mark beside its introduction (before (i)); sub-parts sum to 5 but Q9 total of 8 implies (b)=6, so marks_mismatch is flagged and the intro part carries 1 mark. Q10's single part (a) kept under Q10. Q8 option figure crops include the printed option letter. Handwritten solution quirks: Q12(a) k written as 240 (read 240); Q13(c) alternative writes 583 200 then uses 5 832 000 (5 832 000 used); Q12(c)(iii) answer given as '3 min' only although the graph also shows t = 6 min; Q10(a)(i) hand-drawn diagram labels D-B edge as 30 where the table gives 32. Solution marks breakdown not given in the sheet. No old_syllabus / standard_topic set.
